market_context.summary:
Two independent shocks drove last week and they partly contradict each other. A cooler-than-expected CPI around Aug 12 cut the odds of a Fed HIKE - 2026's regime is hike-risk, not cut-hope - which ended a five-month gold correction and gave gold miners their best week in years (+20%+). Then on Friday Aug 14 the Strait of Hormuz re-escalated with fresh tanker attacks, taking NYMEX WTI September to an $82.40 settle, +5% on the week. Sustained $82 crude is inflationary and undercuts the very no-hike premise gold just rallied on; that tension is the most important thing in this week's tape. Note Hormuz is a two-sided headline generator - earlier in the same week the market traded a prospective US-Iran agreement and oil fell on it.

Friday's tape was rotation within risk, not de-risking: precious metals and energy led (GDX +1.9%, USO +1.3%, GLD +0.6%) while long duration and high-beta growth lagged (TLT -0.67%, ARKK -1.8%), with IWM +0.5% against QQQ -0.14%. That is a reflation/inflation-hedge rotation.

Rates eased at both ends with the curve steepening (10y 4.63% from 4.68%, 2y 4.15% from 4.20%, 10y-2y +0.51 from +0.48). But effective fed funds at 3.63% against a 2y at 4.15% means the front end prices no near-term cuts and some hike premium - a hawkish-repricing tape.

The week ahead has three genuinely independent drivers: a concentrated US-consumer verdict Aug 18-20 (HD and LOW on housing, WMT/TGT/TJX/ROST on the staples-discretionary split), Wednesday's FOMC minutes from the July 28-29 meeting where THREE officials dissented in favour of a hike, and RDDT's S&P 500 inclusion before Tuesday's open. Jackson Hole follows Aug 27-29, Chair Warsh's first keynote there, which is why positioning stays tight.
